headline: US stocks closed higher as value and healthcare rotation followed earnings beats while oil and Treasury yields eased amid weak housing data
raw_text:
- The Dow Jones Industrial Average ($DJI) rose about 530 points to 52,496, the S&P 500 ($SPX) gained roughly 0.3% to 7,713, and the Nasdaq Composite ($COMP) was little changed at 26,425, with roughly three-quarters of S&P 500 ($SPX) names advancing and the Russell 2000 (IWM) up about 1.7%.
- Healthcare hit a record high as Eli Lilly (LLY) climbed about 3.6% after RBC reiterated it as the preferred pharma stock with a $1,500 price target, and UnitedHealth (UNH), Merck (MRK), Amgen (AMGN), Pfizer (PFE), and Johnson & Johnson (JNJ) each advanced more than 2%.
- 3M (MMM) gained roughly 6% after beating earnings estimates, raising its full-year forecast, and expanding a data-center partnership with Amazon (AMZN) via a warrant deal.
- Boeing (BA) slipped about 0.5% after the Federal Aviation Administration certified its 737 MAX-10 jet.
- General Motors (GM) fell about 6.8% despite a Q3 earnings beat and a $20 billion buyback announcement as commodity inflation and input-cost headwinds pressured the stock.
- Steel Dynamics (STLD) declined after missing quarterly profit estimates.
- Energy underperformed as Brent crude (@QA) slipped 1.2% to $108.23 per barrel, giving back part of a recent run to a five-month high amid Mideast tensions and diplomatic efforts.
- The 10-year Treasury yield eased 4 basis points to 5.10% while pending home sales dropped 7.3% in September.
- After the close, Netflix (NFLX) reported Q3 results that beat revenue estimates, with shares down about 5% in extended-hours trading.
- SpaceX (SPCX) also reported Q3 results after the bell, beating revenue estimates, with shares off about 0.9% in early after-hours trading.
